source.title: Revisiting the 16x Pretraining Compute Gap between Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models
source.authors: Guang-Han Wang; B. He; Zhan Shi; Benoît Dumoulin; Han-Qing Lu; V. Kuleshov

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study conducts IsoFLOP scaling sweeps and reports fitted compute-optimal loss laws, a held-out compute test, and results on how protocol choices change the measured compute gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many individual IsoFLOP cells and decoder-depth sweep results. Rows below capture the fitted scaling laws, held-out extrapolation checks, decoder-depth summary, and downstream scaling comparison; individual per-cell NLLs are not repeated.
record.test_reason: The study applies the Hoffmann IsoFLOP protocol to an ARM and nine diffusion LM variants. It fits compute-optimal loss power laws over 5 budgets, checks them at a held-out 3×10^20 budget, sweeps decoder depth, and relates downstream accuracy to NLL. These results bear directly on V1, V2, V4, V6 and V7 in a new setting (diffusion LMs). It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the 16× figure overstates the DLM–ARM pretraining gap: DUEL scoring gives 12.8×, BD3LM/E2D2 give 7.8× at b=32, and smaller blocks give 4.6× at b=8 and 3.0× at b=4. They add that held-out absolute losses sit about 1.1% above the pure power law, which they attribute to a small irreducible term. They keep the pure form and treat the exponents as local to the fitted range. The between-variant gap is reproduced and is insensitive to this misspecification.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an IsoFLOP size ladder and compute-optimal loss fitting similar to prior scaling studies, but compares diffusion variants with an ARM, uses DUEL and ELBO readouts, block sizes, encoder–decoder models, exact FLOP accounting, and an in-range compute-multiple readout.
record.method_sensitivity: The compute multiple varies with evaluation measure (ELBO versus DUEL), model design (MDM, BD3LM, E2D2), and block size. The optimal decoder fraction varies primarily with block size. The paper also reports a shared held-out deviation for pure power-law fits.

fits_no_version.finding: The optimal decoder fraction of E2D2 depends mainly on block size (+0.043 per doubling of b). Dependence on N is negligible and on C weak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal encoder/decoder split in encoder–decoder diffusion LMs is set by block size, not scale.

record.problems: All experiments use a single fixed random seed. The held-out budget was not run for block size 8. DUEL is measured only under the top-1 confidence sampler. Experiments share one learning-rate and batch-size configuration. The pure power-law fits miss held-out absolute losses by about 1.1%, and the authors say the exponents should be treated as local to the fitted range. Several downstream results are shown in figures, while exact per-benchmark values are in the appendix.
record.rows_left_out: The individual IsoFLOP loss cells in Tables 17–26 and the full decoder-depth sweep tables are not listed row by row; they contain far more than 60 distinct runs. The fitted-law rows and decoder-depth summary rows capture the reported aggregate results most directly relevant to the claim. Table 15's per-benchmark accuracy values are also omitted; Figure 6 and the text provide the cross-variant mean-accuracy trend.

untested.parts: Separate power laws in N or D. Behaviour over several orders of magnitude: the fits span only 1.2 decades of compute.
Extrapolation by orders of magnitude: the held-out budget is only 3× the largest fitted budget.
All of V3: no N_opt(C) or D_opt(C) allocation exponents are fitted.
Width, depth, aspect ratio and other shape changes beyond the encoder/decoder split at fixed total depth.
All of V5: other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested.
Fitted downstream scaling laws and loss-to-accuracy mappings; only orderings and trends are reported.
Data, training schedule and parameter-count conventions. FLOP counting is changed but fits are not compared against 6ND.

missing.what: Shared-E irreducible-term fit profile. α_ARM moves from −0.062 (E=0) to −0.147 (E=1.5), the in-sample rms falls from 5.9 to 3.1 m-nats, and the held-out miss is removed.
Loss vs decoder fraction at each (C, N): the magnitude of the shape effect, flat near the optimum and large at extreme splits.
missing.locator: Tables 18–26; Section 4.2 'DUEL basin around L*dec is flat'

missing.what: Benchmarks that do not improve with scale: WinoGrande at chance (50.8%), BoolQ decreasing with compute, COPA too noisy.
Per-budget mean and per-benchmark accuracies, which the rows currently record as figure-only.
In-range vs extrapolating readout of the compute multiple, which differ by up to 22% (MDM DUEL) at 1e20.

record.verdict_notes: The ARM IsoFLOP sweep is essentially a T1 replication of the Chinchilla method; the diffusion variants are a new setting (T3). The fit range is narrow (1.2 decades), a single seed is used, and there is one LR/batch configuration. The V6 support is weakened because benchmarks were screened for rising with compute.

versions.untested_parts: The paper fits compute-optimal loss against training compute, not separate power laws in parameter count or token count with the other quantities non-bottlenecked; it does not establish several-orders-of-magnitude behavior.
The held-out test is at 3×1020 FLOPs, three times the largest fitting budget, not orders of magnitude larger; it tests only ARM and E2D2 at block sizes 16 and 32.
The paper finds compute-optimal sizes within IsoFLOP sweeps but does not fit or report parameter-count and token-count allocation as power laws of compute.
Only encoder–decoder decoder-depth splits are swept; broad changes in width, depth, and other architecture details are not tested.
The study concerns text pretraining and does not test other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer.

Downstream results are zero-shot mean accuracy on eight retained benchmarks and concern the compute-optimal cells of selected variants; the study does not test a broad set of downstream tasks or model families.

The paper tests sensitivity to its evaluation/model-design choices and notes a high-compute deviation from the fitted power law. It does not systematically vary data, training schedules, parameter-count conventions, or all fitting methods.

relation.reason: Its own fitted loss curves, held-out losses, evaluation contrasts, and downstream measurements directly bear on claim versions.

tranche.reason: The study reports direct scaling results in diffusion-model settings using revised likelihood evaluation and model designs. Its principal revision concerns the 16× diffusion–ARM comparison, rather than rejection of scaling laws generally.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase conflates architectures: at b=32, BD3LM gives 9.6× and E2D2 gives 7.8×. All runs use one seed; held-out values are best measured cells from limited size sweeps, not full IsoFLOP optima.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Compute-optimal NLL laws for the tested ARM, MDM, BD3LM, and E2D2 variants over the five fitted budgets
reader_labels.reason: All reported variants have fitted power laws in compute; the paper reports a maximum relative residual of 0.5% within the fitted range (r1–r11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The absolute predictions undershoot measured NLL by 1.07–1.15% for ARM and E2D2, although the ARM–E2D2 gaps are close to predicted; this is only a threefold extension beyond the largest fitted budget (r12–r16).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: E2D2 decoder-depth split sweeps at block sizes 4, 8, 16, and 32
reader_labels.reason: The rule-based decoder split is within 10 m-nats of the best split for 87–100% of grid points, including all compute-optimal columns, in these tested depth-split settings (r17–r20).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Compute-optimal cells of ARM, MDM, BD3LM b=32, and E2D2 b=4 and b=32 on the eight retained benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The reported cross-variant accuracy ordering broadly tracks NLL; orders coincide at the three largest budgets and differ only within noise at the two smallest (r21–r25).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Changes to diffusion evaluation method, model design, and block size
reader_labels.reason: The reported compute multiple changes from 17.8 with ELBO to 12.8 with DUEL and varies across block/model designs; the fitted exponents also differ across variants (r2–r11).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Pure power-law extrapolation to the held-out budget
reader_labels.reason: All three held-out measurements sit 1.07–1.15% above their pure power-law predictions; the authors interpret the common deviation as evidence of a small irreducible term and treat exponents as local to the fitted range (r12–r14).
